A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LaRA-VLA research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulation and real-robot evaluations, CoT ablations, latent-representation analysis, and inference measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds visual-corruption tests and experiments on action pretraining, inference-time reasoning, and EMA.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the annotation pipeline, Qwen3-VL backbone, three-stage curriculum, attention rules, EMA encoder, action expert, and losses. The new component-removal variants are experimental controls; the proposed method remains unchanged.

E1.justification: LIBERO, SimplerEnv, and the four real-robot tasks remain. v2 adds Gaussian-blur and Gaussian-noise evaluation scenarios at two severity levels on both simulation benchmarks, extending input conditions without adding datasets or manipulation tasks.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds an ECoT-style baseline to the real-robot comparison, although ECoT already appeared in v1's latency comparison. New Table 4 evaluates Qwen-GR00T against LaRA-VLA under visual corruption. Comparator membership in the main simulation Tables 2–3 is unchanged.

E3.justification: The original rollout counts and training configurations remain. Added diagnostic protocols specify blur/noise severities, checkpoint evaluation every 5k steps from 35k to 60k, removal of reasoning and future-image tokens at inference, and EMA-on/off evaluation using feature rank.

E4.justification: v2 substantially expands the diagnostic evidence: Table 5 adds visual-only latent CoT; Table 4 and Figure 6 test corruption robustness; Appendix D tests action pretraining, separates training supervision from inference-time reasoning, and examines EMA through feature rank and latent distributions. These address component contributions and stability beyond v1's existing analyses.

E5.justification: Neither version reports seed-based variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests, and the original rollout counts remain unchanged. The new checkpoint averages summarize training progress rather than uncertainty across independent runs.

E6.justification: Main benchmark scores, existing real-robot scores, and latencies remain unchanged. New results include corruption success rates, 63.5% for visual-only CoT, ECoT's 20.8% real-robot average, action-pretraining averages of 60.4% without versus 64.2% with pretraining, and EMA ranks of 6.76 with versus 5.10 without EMA. Section 4.2 also corrects the reported real-robot wins from four tasks to three; existing CoT-ablation values are merely rounded.

T1.justification: The mathematical objectives, EMA update, flow-matching formulation, and associated definitions remain unchanged. The added empirical feature-rank measurement introduces no formal definition, derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, three principal contributions, and conclusion retain their scientific scope. The introduction adds a specific novelty claim relative to Fast-ThinkAct, emphasizing jointly continuous textual and future-oriented visual reasoning and visual supervision of textual latents.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations separating training-induced representation benefits from inference-time reasoning and explaining action pretraining and corruption robustness. Appendix D qualifies the earlier collapse-prevention emphasis: EMA improves diversity and semantic separation but is not necessary to avoid immediate collapse. The efficiency discussion also proposes reasons for outperforming Fast-ThinkAct; Section 5's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds a direct code-repository link and documents the real-robot ECoT-style baseline as an ablated LaRA-VLA configuration. It also specifies corruption parameters and procedures for the new ablations. Existing hyperparameter tables, hardware information, annotation instructions, and prompts are retained.

R1.justification: v2 adds focused positioning against the already cited and evaluated Fast-ThinkAct, including its taxonomy row. It adds references to StarVLA and Bai et al.'s action-error-distribution work and discusses ECoT-lite using an existing reference. The broader related-work coverage remains.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized introduction, results, and efficiency edits, divides related work into numbered subsections, shortens running headers, and adds acknowledgements and Appendix D. The abstract, method exposition, and overall narrative organization remain largely intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the experimental displays with robustness and appendix-ablation tables and new corruption/EMA latent-distribution figures. Figure 5 gains ECoT bars and task-number labels, coordinated with Figure 4; the taxonomy and CoT-ablation tables gain rows. Existing method diagrams, latency plot, and appendix prompts are retained with layout adjustments.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses important evidential gaps in v1 by separating training-only CoT benefits from inference-time reasoning, completing the modality ablation, and testing action pretraining, EMA, and visual corruption. These controls substantially strengthen the central empirical argument and support a more qualified account of EMA. Correcting the all-four-task superiority statement also improves accuracy. Statistical uncertainty remains unreported, but the added diagnostic evidence provides a clear overall quality gain.
